notes: The file half of the Madagascar (2005) port. The game streams 253 MB of serialized levels through a pointer table it fills at startup: on NT it binds the real KERNEL32 async exports, and on Win9x it falls back to its own worker thread and queue -- which is the record of when its completions are allowed to run.

functions.name: ReadFileEx

stub.body: read into the buffer at the OVERLAPPED offset now, record Internal/InternalHigh, signal the OVERLAPPED event, queue the routine for the asking thread

functions.description: The streaming loader's async read. The bytes land now (host memory, no latency to hide); the completion routine is queued and the session runs it on the asking thread at its next switch point, the way a timer callback runs. The game resolves ReadFileEx through a pointer table it binds at startup (0x51dc80: real exports on NT 5+, its own 0x51d860 fallback with a worker thread on 9x), and its 9x worker delivers completions from a worker context, so switch-point delivery is inside the behaviour the game was written against. The game imports no alertable wait (no SleepEx, no *ObjectEx), so the strict alertable-wait rule would mean the routine never runs at all.
functions.evidence: import table (KERNEL32!ReadFileEx at IAT 0x5CA0B0); call through the bound pointer table 0x60D820 set at 0x51DCF5; the 9x fallback 0x51D860 queues to the worker at 0x51CB70, which performs plain ReadFile and delivers completions itself; first probe run reached the loading screen with no missing-shim stop

functions.name: ReadFile
functions.description: The worker thread's own read (0x51CBE2 calls it through 0x60D81C), and the streaming loader's synchronous path: 4-32 KB chunks out of LEVELS\Title.stream on the loading screen.
functions.evidence: trace: SHIMKIT_LOG_FILES shows handle 0x60020 read 29 chunks of 4-32 KB while the loading screen ran
